task.instruction: Find a report on the BBC News website about recent developments in renewable energy technologies in the UK.

final_answer:
I found a BBC News report on a recent UK renewable energy technology development: **"Turning the tides: Could hidden sea power energise our coastal towns?"** by Paul Hastie, BBC Scotland, published 18 October 2026. Link: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8y56y6xg9n9o

The article covers the Swimmer Turbine, a small-scale 50kW tidal generator developed by engineer David Mummery's company, Flex Marine Power. It sits anchored on the seabed, invisible below the surface, and can power about 30 homes. It is built to be cheap and compact. Local fishermen and workers can assemble it from a shipping-container kit of about 20 components and launch it from their own slipway. That contrasts with large tidal projects in Scotland such as Nova Innovation in Shetland, MeyGen in the Pentland Firth and Orbital O2 in Orkney.

The article traces the project's progress:
- A prototype was trialled on Luing in 2015.
- A full-scale test followed at Strangford Narrows in Northern Ireland in 2020.
- The company received £968,000 from the UK government's Energy Entrepreneurs Fund.
- Months of testing on the Isle of Islay took place last year, with locals launching the turbine themselves.
- Mummery plans to return to Islay next year to generate electricity for the island.

Other recent BBC pieces on related topics include:
- "'It's offensively cheap': How solar power is quietly becoming bigger than nuclear" (26 Oct 2026)
- "Bringing landfill into the 21st Century with solar power" (26 Oct 2026)
- "Dales wind farm would 'spoil' view, says former PM" (28 Oct 2026)

judge.rationale: The agent found and cited a BBC News article dated 18 Oct 2026 about UK tidal renewable energy technology, supported by the final page content.
